text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah. Yeah, I can hear you.
B: Okay. Erm, I'm Gemma.
A: Kayleigh.
B: So we just sort of talk, yeah? For three minutes.
A: Suppose so. I'm not being funny but I'm only doing it for the money, to be fair.
B: Same, honestly. Student bursary doesn't exactly stretch.
A: Student? I had you down as a nurse, from your picture. The scrubs on the airer, like.
B: Yeah, nearly. Final year, so I'm on placement full time on a medical ward. Long days, nights, all of it. I did three years as a healthcare assistant before that, so I sort of know the drill.
A: I'm a carer. Care home, older people. Twelve-hour days mostly.
B: Oh, so you're in it as well. Did you just come off one? You look how I feel.
A: Cheers.
B: Sorry, that came out wrong. I just meant knackered.
A: No, you're alright, I am knackered. Third one this week. I've still got my tunic on under this, I haven't even changed.
B: Is it a decent place?
A: Honestly? No. It's badly run, the pay's a joke, and the seniors just sit in the office doing their notes while we're running round doing everything. And then they'll have a go at you 'cause you're two minutes late for handover, when the parking's a nightmare and there's nowhere to put your car anyway. Do you know what I mean? Like, give me somewhere to park and I'll be on time.
B: Yeah. When I was an HCA it was the same, the staff car park was full by seven. I don't drive in London anyway, the bus from Catford takes forever. But the seniors thing, yeah, I get that.
A: I'd go agency tomorrow for an extra pound an hour, to be fair.
B: Why don't you?
A: Dunno really.
B: Fair enough.
A: Erm, my mum has my daughter after school, so I sort of need regular shifts. Agency's all over the place.
B: How old's your daughter?
A: Ten. Lacey. My mum does most of the pick-ups, she's ten minutes away, so that's a godsend. What about you, you got kids?
B: No. Everyone keeps asking, both families. My husband wants a dog first and I keep saying no to that as well.
A: Dogs are more work than kids, some of them.
B: That's what I said. We've got a one-bed flat above a dry cleaner's, where's it going to go?
A: Do you like it though, the nursing? 'Cause I started my Level 3 twice and never finished, it was the written bits. I couldn't be doing essays.
B: The hands-on bit, yeah, I love it. Cannulas, obs, when someone's going off and you've got to be quick. The essays I hate. I've got one due Friday I haven't started, so, you know. I'm not the person to ask about writing stuff.
A: At least you're getting a proper job out of it though. Band whatever.
B: Band 5, hopefully. It's still not loads, to be honest. But better than a bursary.
A: Anything's better than what we get. I picked up a meal deal and an energy drink on the way home and that's my tea.
B: That's me on nights. Meal deal and a Twix out the vending machine at four in the morning.
A: Living the dream, innit.
B: Honestly. What did you think of that puzzle thing at the start? I didn't get the last one.
A: I just guessed. I wasn't sitting there for ages, I've been up since half five.
B: Yeah, I gave up on it as well, I was just—
